source_title: During Balen Shah's first India visit, Nepal to seek aid, investment
source_excerpt: NEW DELHI: Nepal will seek Indian financial assistance for flood reconstruction, fresh investment in hydropower and faster implementation of stalled infrastructure projects during prime minister Balen Shah's proposed visit to India in late Nov. Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri is expected in Kathmandu on Nov 4 to prepare the agenda for Shah's first bilateral foreign visit, which comes after months of diplomatic friction, including a postponed visit by Misri and differences over Lipulekh.Kathmandu wants the visit to produce concrete financial commitments, stronger energy cooperation and progress on projects that have remained pending despite earlier agreements. Both countries are also exploring infrastructure projects that could be inaugurated or launched during the visit.Shah's trip is expected in the latter half of Nov, although the dates have not been formally announced. New Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela is expected in Kathmandu on Nov 3, a day before Misri's proposed arrival. The foreign secretary is expected to hold discussions with senior Nepali officials to finalise the agenda for the prime ministerial visit.A source from the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) told TOI, âThe PM wants the visit to deliver tangible results, particularly on flood reconstruction, hydropower and projects that have remained stalled for years. Our priority is to secure commitments that can be implemented, rather than make fresh announcements. While political differences exist between our nations, economic cooperation should not be held hostage to them; preparatory talks will help outline clear paths forward where both sides can pragmatically align.âThe source added, âNepal has enormous hydropower potential, but investment and implementation have not kept pace. We want clearer timelines for pending projects and stronger commitments on electricity trade and cross-border infrastructure, ensuring that mutual economic benefits override temporary diplomatic hurdles.âReconstruction assistance is expected to be a major priority following the floods in Aug, which damaged roads, bridges and other infrastructure. Kathmandu is seeking Indian grants and concessional loans to rebuild affected facilities and strengthen connectivity in vulnerable areas.Cross-border connectivity is another priority. The two sides are expected to discuss integrated check posts, border bridges and petroleum pipelines, including projects that have faced delays despite earlier understandings.The proposed visit follows a shift in RSP's public messaging towards India. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit in New Delhi in Oct, Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle said, âThere was a time when nationalism in Nepal was associated with anti-India sentiment.
